fields.description: The bank row this match belongs to.
fields.label: Import Row

fields.description: Denormalised from the row so a batch's whole match set reads in one query.
fields.label: Import Batch

fields.description: Denormalised from the row. Half of the unique constraint that makes settlement idempotent across batches.
fields.label: Transfer Id

fields.description: The matched record's doctype: Project Payments (read-only reconciliation) or Project Expenses / Non Project Expenses (settlement).
fields.label: Target Doctype

fields.description: The target's own amount at match time. Kept so a fan-out group's sum can be compared against the bank amount without re-reading every target.
fields.label: Target Amount

fields.description: Always Settled. This table records SETTLEMENTS ONLY -- a row here means money was written: a payment or expense marked Paid, or an expense created at Paid. The v2 kind 'Reconciled' (matched, nothing written) was retired at the v3 reversal, because a suggestion and a settlement addressing the same record would contend for the (transfer_id, target_doctype, target_name) unique constraint -- which IS this feature's idempotency guarantee. The field is kept as a Select rather than dropped so the intent stays legible and a future write kind has somewhere to go.
fields.label: Match Kind

fields.description: How the match was found. Bank reference = the strong key (normalized bank_reference_no equals the target's normalized utr). Vendor+amount+date = the weak second pass, needed because 12.6% of Paid payments carry a UTR that is not a bank reference. Manual = a person chose the target outright.
fields.label: Match Basis

fields.description: Who confirmed the match (frappe.session.user). Data, not Link, per the house convention for actor fields.
fields.label: Matched By
